name: Methi Paratha
steps: Pick fenugreek leaves from tough stems, wash well and dry thoroughly. Chop finely; reserve 30 g flour for rolling.
Mix remaining flour with leaves, salt, carom seeds, turmeric and chilli powder. Add curd, 10 g ghee and water gradually to make soft dough.
Rest covered for 20 minutes, then divide into eight balls. Roll one ball into a small disc and spread a thin film of ghee.
Fold the disc in half, grease lightly and fold again into a triangle. Roll gently with reserved flour to about 3 mm thick.
Heat a heavy tawa over medium-high heat. Cook a paratha for 60–90 seconds until bubbles appear, then turn and brush with a little ghee.
Turn again, grease the second side and press the edges. Cook 2–3 minutes more until browned on both sides with no damp dough at the edges.
tips: Keep unused dough covered so the surface does not dry out.
notes: Makes eight breads, two per serving. Serve freshly cooked with a curry or curd.
